library(survival)
library(survminer)

frameworks <- c("Drews", "Steele", "Tao")

# Scope

Reviewer 2: *"Adding one scalar baseline (fraction of genome altered, ploidy,
WGD, or an HRD score) to the clustering, survival, and prediction comparisons
would answer the obvious question of how much structure requires signatures at
all."*

We use fraction genome altered (FGA), the most general of the suggested
measures, in the three comparisons, with the same patients, saved clusters and
splits as the manuscript.

Scripts (each can also be run on its own from the repository root):

| Step | Script | Output |
|---|---|---|
| FGA download | `code/revision/13_fetch_fga.R` | `data/processed/fga_pancanatlas.csv` |
| Prediction | `code/revision/14_fga_prediction.R` | `results/revision/prediction/fixed/fga_baseline/` |
| Survival | `code/revision/15_fga_survival.R` | `results/revision/fga_baseline/survival_cox.csv` |
| Clustering | `code/revision/16_fga_clustering.R` | `results/revision/fga_baseline/clustering_fga_*.csv` |

This notebook reads the saved FGA values and prediction results, and reruns
the survival and clustering analyses, which take a few seconds. To refresh the
FGA download (internet needed) or the prediction models (about 15 minutes),
run the corresponding scripts first.

# FGA data

FGA from the cBioPortal TCGA PanCanAtlas 2018 studies (sample attribute
`FRACTION_GENOME_ALTERED`): total length of segments with |segment mean| ≥ 0.2
divided by the total length of the measured segments. One sample per patient:
the primary tumour or, when there is none, the metastasis (365 SKCM patients,
whose TCGA samples are mostly metastatic; without them FGA would be missing for
most melanomas, not at random).

FGA is computed from the segment means without purity correction, so tumours
of low purity tend to have a lower FGA. The Cox models below adjust for purity;
the FGA-only classifier does not.

Same tumour sample as the signatures: checked against the ASCAT tumour
barcodes of the TCGA SNP6 profiles (`Metadata_TCGA_ASCAT_penalty70.rds`, not
in the repository).
- Drews: 6134 of 6135 clustered patients with FGA have the same sample; the
  exception is one SKCM patient (signatures on the primary, FGA on the
  metastasis).
- Tao: by construction, since the Tao preprocessing keeps only primary samples.
- Steele: an estimated 42 of 9402 differ (0.4%), assuming the same ASCAT
  profiles.

```{r fga-data}
fga_table <- read.csv("data/processed/fga_pancanatlas.csv")
fga <- setNames(fga_table$fga, fga_table$patient)
writeLines(readLines("data/processed/fga_pancanatlas_provenance.txt"))
summary(fga)
ggplot(fga_table, aes(fga)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey60") +
  labs(x = "Fraction genome altered", y = "Tumours") + theme_minimal()
```

## Coverage on the manuscript cohorts

```{r coverage}
cl <- new.env(); load("data/processed/clustering_data.RData", envir = cl)
sv <- new.env(); load("data/processed/surv_data.RData", envir = sv)
fits <- c(Drews = "mc_drew_active_4", Steele = "mc_steele_active_4", Tao = "mc_tao_active_4")
survs <- c(Drews = "drew_f", Steele = "steele_f", Tao = "tao_f")
coverage <- do.call(rbind, lapply(frameworks, function(fw) {
  cls <- cl[[fits[fw]]]$classification
  surv_ids <- rownames(sv[[survs[fw]]])
  m <- read.csv(file.path("results/revision/prediction/fixed/archived", fw, "manifests.csv"),
                colClasses = c(split_id = "character"))
  pred_ids <- m$patient_id[m$split_id == "0"]
  f <- function(ids) sprintf("%d / %d (%.1f%%)", sum(!is.na(fga[ids])), length(ids),
                             100 * mean(!is.na(fga[ids])))
  data.frame(framework = fw, clustering = f(names(cls)), survival = f(surv_ids),
             prediction_cluster1_2 = f(pred_ids))
}))
knitr::kable(coverage)
```

# 1. Clustering: FGA across the signature-based clusters

- **R2**: share of the differences in FGA between tumours explained by the
  cluster they belong to (1 = each cluster has a single FGA value; 0 = all
  clusters have the same FGA distribution).
- **Beyond cancer type** (partial R2): FGA depends strongly on cancer type, and
  clusters are partly related to cancer type. After removing the part of FGA
  explained by cancer type, this is the share of the remaining variation
  explained by the clusters, i.e. how much the cluster says about FGA among
  tumours of the same type.

```{r clustering}
source("code/revision/16_fga_clustering.R")
```

```{r clustering-plot, fig.height = 3.5}
long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(frameworks, function(fw) {
  cls <- cl[[fits[fw]]]$classification
  data.frame(framework = fw, cluster = paste("Cluster", cls), fga = unname(fga[names(cls)]))
}))
long <- long[!is.na(long$fga), ]
long$framework <- factor(long$framework, frameworks)
r2 <- read.csv("results/revision/fga_baseline/clustering_fga_variance.csv")
r2$label <- sprintf("R2 = %.2f\n(beyond cancer type %.2f)", r2$r2_cluster,
                    r2$partial_r2_cluster_given_cancer_type)
r2$framework <- factor(r2$framework, frameworks)
ggplot(long, aes(cluster, fga, fill = framework)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = .3, alpha = .6) +
  geom_text(data = r2, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.2, size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(~framework, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fraction genome altered") + theme_minimal()
```

# 2. Survival: Figure 7 models with FGA

Cancer-type-stratified Cox models of Figure 7 (cluster + age + purity), on the
patients with FGA, without FGA and with FGA. The question is how much of the
association of the clusters with outcome remains when patients with similar
FGA are compared. The reference is always the model without FGA on the same
patients (`figure7_fga_n`), so that the only difference is FGA; the Figure 7
values on all patients are listed in the table for comparison.

- **FGA spline (main)**: FGA enters as a flexible curve (penalized spline,
  `pspline`, 4 df). The likelihood-ratio test below shows that the effect of FGA
  is clearly non-linear.
- **FGA linear (sensitivity analysis)**: FGA enters as a straight line on the
  log-hazard scale. The conclusions on the clusters are the same with either
  specification (table "Spline vs linear" below).

Holm correction as in Figure 7 (all cluster terms of the six models, separately
for each model set).

```{r survival}
source("code/revision/15_fga_survival.R")
cox <- read.csv("results/revision/fga_baseline/survival_cox.csv")
```

```{r survival-forest, fig.height = 4}
labels <- c(figure7_fga_n = "Without FGA", with_fga = "FGA linear",
            with_fga_spline = "FGA spline (main)")
f <- cox[cox$term == "cluster2" & cox$model %in% names(labels), ]
f$model <- factor(labels[f$model], rev(labels))
f$row <- factor(paste(f$framework, f$endpoint), rev(unique(paste(f$framework, f$endpoint))))
f$p_label <- sprintf("p = %.2g, Holm %.2g", f$p, f$p_holm)
ggplot(f, aes(hr, row, colour = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), height = .25,
                 position = position_dodge(width = .6)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = .6), size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey40", "#fdae61", "#d7191c"), name = NULL,
                      breaks = labels) +
  labs(x = "Hazard ratio, Cluster 2 vs Cluster 1 (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r survival-table}
tab <- cox[cox$term == "cluster2" & cox$model %in% c("figure7", names(labels)), ]
tab$hr_ci <- sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", tab$hr, tab$lower, tab$upper)
tab$p <- signif(tab$p, 2); tab$p_holm <- signif(tab$p_holm, 2)
knitr::kable(tab[, c("framework", "endpoint", "model", "n", "events", "hr_ci", "p", "p_holm")],
             row.names = FALSE)
# Spline vs linear: Cluster 2 vs 1 on the same patients, and the share of the
# log hazard ratio removed by adding FGA (reference: figure7_fga_n).
wide <- function(m) {
  x <- cox[cox$term == "cluster2" & cox$model == m, ]
  setNames(x[, c("hr", "p_holm")], paste(m, c("hr", "p_holm"), sep = "_"))
}
key <- cox[cox$term == "cluster2" & cox$model == "figure7_fga_n", c("framework", "endpoint")]
sens <- cbind(key, wide("figure7_fga_n"), wide("with_fga_spline"), wide("with_fga"))
sens$log_hr_reduction_spline <- 1 - log(sens$with_fga_spline_hr) / log(sens$figure7_fga_n_hr)
sens$log_hr_reduction_linear <- 1 - log(sens$with_fga_hr) / log(sens$figure7_fga_n_hr)
knitr::kable(sens, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Spline vs linear: Cluster 2 vs 1 HR, Holm p and log-HR reduction")
nl <- unique(cox[, c("framework", "endpoint", "fga_nonlinearity_p")])
knitr::kable(nl, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Likelihood-ratio test, spline vs linear FGA")
knitr::kable(cox[cox$model == "fga_only", c("framework", "endpoint", "n", "hr", "lower", "upper", "p")],
             row.names = FALSE, digits = 3, caption = "FGA alone (linear, HR per 0.1 increase)")
```

## Hazard ratio tables (as in notebook 03)

All clusters (reference: Cluster 1), same patients with FGA, without FGA and
with FGA as a spline. Unadjusted p-values; the Holm-adjusted values are in the
table above.

```{r survival-gtsummary}
library(gtsummary)
hr_tables <- list(); headers <- character()
for (fw in names(spec)) for (ep in c("OS", "PFI")) {
  s <- spec[[fw]]
  d <- cox_data(s[[1]], s[[2]]$classification, s[[3]], paste0(ep, ".time"), ep)
  d <- d[!is.na(d$fga10), ]
  without <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ cluster + age + purity + strata(cancer_type), data = d)
  with_spline <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ cluster + pspline(fga10, df = 4) + age + purity +
                         strata(cancer_type), data = d)
  hr_tables[[length(hr_tables) + 1]] <- tbl_merge(
    list(tbl_regression(without, exp = TRUE, include = "cluster") %>% bold_p(t = 0.05),
         tbl_regression(with_spline, exp = TRUE, include = "cluster") %>% bold_p(t = 0.05)),
    tab_spanner = c("**Without FGA**", "**With FGA (spline)**"))
  headers <- c(headers, paste0(fw, " - ", ep, " (n = ", nrow(d), ")"))
}
tbl_stack(hr_tables, group_header = headers)
```

## Shape of the FGA effect

How the risk changes with FGA in the spline models (OS), at equal cluster, age
and purity. y axis: hazard relative to a tumour with the median FGA (log
scale; 0.7 = 30% lower risk, 1.2 = 20% higher); band: 95% CI. Risk rises from
FGA 0 to about 0.45 and then flattens; the right end is uncertain (few tumours
with very high FGA). A straight line averages the rise and the plateau and
under-adjusts at low FGA, where the Cluster 2 tumours lie (median FGA
0.11-0.17).

```{r spline-shape, fig.height = 3}
shape <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(spec), function(fw) {
  s <- spec[[fw]]
  d <- cox_data(s[[1]], s[[2]]$classification, s[[3]], "OS.time", "OS")
  d <- d[!is.na(d$fga10), ]
  fit <- coxph(Surv(time, event) ~ cluster + pspline(fga10, df = 4) + age + purity +
                 strata(cancer_type), data = d)
  tp <- termplot(fit, terms = 2, se = TRUE, plot = FALSE)[[1]]
  ref <- tp$y[which.min(abs(tp$x - median(d$fga10)))]
  data.frame(framework = fw, fga = tp$x / 10, hr = exp(tp$y - ref),
             lower = exp(tp$y - ref - 1.96 * tp$se), upper = exp(tp$y - ref + 1.96 * tp$se))
}))
ggplot(shape, aes(fga, hr, colour = framework, fill = framework)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = .15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() + geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~framework) + scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Fraction genome altered", y = "Relative hazard (OS)") + theme_minimal()
```

# 3. Prediction: multi-omic vs FGA-only classifiers

Cluster 1 versus Cluster 2, same patients and splits (reconstructed original
split and 20 repeated cancer-type-stratified 80/20 splits). The FGA-only model
was tuned once on the split-0 training set with the original grid. Balanced
accuracy (mean of the proportions of Cluster 1 and Cluster 2 patients correctly
classified) is used because the Cluster 1 F1 depends on the class proportions;
F1 is in the table. The 2% of patients without an FGA value are kept, with the
missing value passed to XGBoost, so that the cohorts and splits are identical.

The table also lists the expression-only classifiers. For Tao, FGA alone
performs as well as expression alone. The difference between the multi-omic
classifier and FGA therefore comes from methylation and purity, and purity is
itself estimated from copy number (Reviewer 2, comment 1). The comparison
without purity is pending.

```{r prediction}
models <- c(archived = "Multi-omic", expression_only = "Expression only", fga_baseline = "FGA only")
bal <- function(tp, fp, fn, tn) (tp / (tp + fn) + tn / (tn + fp)) / 2
splits <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(v) do.call(rbind, lapply(frameworks, function(fw) {
  m <- read.csv(file.path("results/revision/prediction/fixed", v, fw, "split_metrics.csv"),
                colClasses = c(split_id = "character"))
  b <- read.csv(file.path("results/revision/prediction/fixed", v, fw, "bootstrap.csv"),
                colClasses = c(split_id = "character"))
  b <- b[b$split_id == "0", ]
  ci <- quantile(bal(b$tp, b$fp, b$fn, b$tn), c(.025, .975))
  data.frame(model = models[[v]], framework = fw, split_id = m$split_id,
             balanced_accuracy = bal(m$tp, m$fp, m$fn, m$tn), f1 = m$f1, trivial_f1 = m$trivial_f1,
             auroc = m$auroc, lower = ci[[1]], upper = ci[[2]])
}))))
plotted <- splits[splits$model != "Expression only", ]
lanes <- rev(as.vector(t(outer(frameworks, models[c("archived", "fga_baseline")], paste))))
plotted$y <- match(paste(plotted$framework, plotted$model), lanes)
s0 <- plotted[plotted$split_id == "0", ]; rep <- plotted[plotted$split_id != "0", ]
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = rep, aes(balanced_accuracy, y - .15, colour = framework),
             position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = .05, seed = 1), size = .9, alpha = .6) +
  geom_errorbarh(data = s0, aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper, y = y + .15, colour = framework), height = .1) +
  geom_point(data = s0, aes(balanced_accuracy, y + .15, colour = framework, shape = model),
             fill = "white", size = 2.2) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`Multi-omic` = 23, `FGA only` = 22), name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_along(lanes), labels = lanes) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Balanced accuracy (points: 20 repeated splits; symbol and bar: original split, 95% CI)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r prediction-table}
summ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(splits, list(splits$model, splits$framework)), function(x) {
  o <- x[x$split_id == "0", ]; r <- x[x$split_id != "0", ]
  data.frame(framework = o$framework, model = o$model,
             split0_balanced_accuracy = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", o$balanced_accuracy, o$lower, o$upper),
             median_balanced_accuracy = round(median(r$balanced_accuracy), 2),
             split0_f1 = round(o$f1, 2), trivial_f1 = round(o$trivial_f1, 2),
             median_auroc = round(median(r$auroc), 2))
}))
summ <- summ[order(match(summ$framework, frameworks), match(summ$model, models)), ]
knitr::kable(summ, row.names = FALSE)
```
